official_common_error_matrix.candidate: all-game thread fan-out causing CPU contention and concurrent memory pressure
official_common_error_matrix.evidence: The official Swarm created all agents and started one thread per game. With the CPU-heavy GenericAGIRuntime, the 25-thread public run slowed every agent to 0.05-0.11 fps and kept all agents alive concurrently. The one-active-game correction preserved behavior while restoring 0.69-4.10 fps and closing the scorecard.

root_cause.statement: GenericAGIRuntime was incorrectly routed through the framework's all-games-at-once Swarm. That orchestration is acceptable for the lightweight sample agent but causes severe contention for this CPU-heavy runtime on Kaggle's four-core CPU allocation, keeps all game state and thread stacks live together, and materially increases the chance that the private scorecard never reaches collectible closure.
root_cause.why_not_format: The third submission used the corrected official format and failed identically, so format mismatch is not a sufficient explanation.
root_cause.why_not_runtime_limit: No shorter undocumented limit is assumed; the correction removes contention and concurrent residency rather than reducing the permitted computation.
